The liquidation of my bank by Puerto Rican banking regulators has been a complete disaster. First, the OCIF Commissioner had no legitimate regulatory reason to put the bank into receivership, as none of the customers' accounts were at risk, and superior alternatives were available that would have fully protected customers and allowed uninterrupted access to their deposits. 

But after almost 4.5 years of complete incompetence and regulatory failure, very few customers have received anything, most will eventually receive only a fraction of what they are owed, and many may end up losing 100% of the value of their accounts due to gross negligence and outright theft. This is a perfect example of the utter failure of government and why the biggest threats to our property come from the public, not the private sector.
